title: Sausage Casserole
subtitle: Pork sausages braised with tomatoes, peppers, and beans
excerpt: Pork sausages browned and then simmered in a thick tomato and red pepper sauce with cannellini beans. It comes together in one pan in under an hour and reheats well the next day.
sourceNotes: One-pan sausage braises appear in British weeknight cookery from the post-war period, influenced by Italian and Spanish sausage-and-tomato combinations. The addition of canned beans is a British adaptation that makes the dish more substantial without extending the cooking time.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze once cooled completely. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat over medium heat until piping hot.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily in a wider, deeper casserole dish.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day once the sauce has thickened and the flavours have settled.

glossaryTerms.definition: A slow-cooking method where food is first browned in fat, then cooked with a small amount of liquid in a covered pan. The liquid and steam combine to tenderise the food while the covered pan concentrates the flavour.

content.text: in a thick tomato and red pepper sauce with white beans. The sausages brown first to build flavour in the pan, then simmer uncovered until the sauce reduces around them. It is a proper, filling weeknight supper from one pan, and it reheats better than most things.

items.prepNote: one 400 g tin, drained and rinsed

content.text: Heat {{rapeseed-oil}} of oil in a wide, deep frying pan or casserole over medium-high heat. Add the {{sausages-pork}} of sausages and cook, turning occasionally, for 8 to 10 minutes until browned all over. Remove and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion and red pepper to the pan and cook in the sausage fat for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for another minute.
Pour in {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned chopped tomatoes. Add the thyme sprigs and stir to combine. Return the sausages to the pan, nestling them into the sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the sausages are cooked through.
Stir in {{cannellini-beans}} of drained cannellini beans. Cook for a further 5 minutes until the beans are heated through and the sauce clings to them. Remove the thyme sprigs, taste, and season.

rows.symptom: Sauce is too thin after 20 minutes
rows.cause: Too much liquid from the tomatoes, or pan too small for the heat to circulate
rows.fix: Increase the heat slightly and stir more frequently. A wide pan loses moisture faster than a deep one; switch to a wider pan if you have one.

rows.symptom: Sausages split and fall apart during simmering
rows.cause: Pricked before cooking, or heat too high
rows.fix: Do not prick sausages before cooking. Keep the simmer gentle; rapid boiling toughens the skin and can burst cheaper sausages.

content.text: Sausage casseroles in British cooking developed in the second half of the twentieth century as tinned tomatoes and supermarket sausages became standard items. The dish borrows from Italian and Spanish sausage braises but has settled into its own form: thicker sauce, white beans rather than pulses, and a British pork banger as the centrepiece. It is one of the first one-pan suppers most home cooks learn to make.
